Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Latency + 5xx spike hitting Checkout (prod) — need immediate visibility

Monica —

We're seeing sustained tail latency on Redwood endpoints serving our Checkout flow (region: us-west-2) starting ~08:45 PDT. Percentiles: p50 ~180ms (normal), p95 jumped to 1.2s -> 3.6s, p99 to 7.8s. Concerningly, 5xx errors climbed from ~0.02% to 1.3% across the last 20 minutes, and two critical customer payments failed (IDs redacted).

We attached a short error snapshot and a trace log from the agent (svc_trace.log). Can you confirm whether this is a model-side regression, infra saturation, or a routing/fallback loop? SwiftPay is routing live traffic through Redwood dedicated pool. This is causing immediate customer impact.

Please advise next steps and whether you can stand up an exec bridge — our VP Product is requesting an update.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Head of Integrations, SwiftPay

Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx spike hitting Checkout (prod) — ops checks

Looping in quick ops checks we ran:
- Host-level GPU util on dedicated pool spiked 74% -> 98% at 08:43; memory and IO normal.
- Serving runtime shows increased KV-cache churn for sequence lengths matching SwiftPay traffic patterns (batch size skewed higher).
- There are repeated model variant fallbacks to a quantized variant between 08:40-08:52; fallback rate correlates with 5xx increase.

Immediate mitigations we can try (15–20 mins):
1) Route SwiftPay traffic to a warmed standby replica pool (lower batch concurrency) — minimal risk, small throughput hit.
2) Pin to the earlier model version (v2.3-stable) to avoid fallback loop if it's model-variant-related.
3) Apply temporary rate shaping to reduce peak batching for long sequences.

Attaching svc_trace.log excerpt and a brief ops note. I'll stand by on the bridge.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole

Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:31:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Latency + 5xx spike hitting Checkout (prod) — proposed escalation plan

Team —

Thanks for the triage. Proposed immediate play (I will own execution):
- Action A (5 mins): cut a routing rule to switch SwiftPay to standby pool (safe fallback), validate error rate returns to baseline.
- Action B (10 mins): if errors persist, rollback the last runtime config flip (we have a canary change at 08:12) to v2.3-stable for that customer cohort.
- Action C (20 mins): enable request-prefix KV caching for SwiftPay's common prompt prefix (should reduce KV churn).

I'll join the exec bridge and loop Vivek for approval if we need transient capacity scaling (burst GPUs). Laura, Monica — please prepare a crisp customer note explaining immediate mitigation and expected window (45–90 mins) and promise a joint postmortem within 48 hours.

-David
David Kim
VP, Engineering Operations | Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com

Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: SwiftPay production: immediate mitigation & ETA (09:40 PDT)

Olivia —

Quick update from the bridge: our ops team observed a fallback/variant churn coincident with increased batch concurrency that caused requests to hit a less stable codepath. Actions taken now:
- Routed SwiftPay traffic to a warmed standby pool (expecting visible improvement in p95 within 5–10 minutes).
- Rolling pin to v2.3-stable paused; we will only rollback if the routing does not reduce errors.
- Engineering is enabling prefix-KV caching for the Checkout flow to cut downstream token work.

Expected customer-visible window: 45–90 minutes for full normalization. We will provide live telemetry snapshots to you at 10:00 PDT and again at 11:00 PDT.

We will also follow up with a technical incident summary and corrective action plan within 48 hours. If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute exec sync at 2:00 PDT today to run through impact and compensating controls.

Apologies for the disruption — prioritizing a conservative approach to avoid repeated fallbacks.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
